A. To My Critics
time limit per test
1 second
memory limit per test
256 megabytes

Suneet has three digits a, b, and c.

Since math isn't his strongest point, he asks you to determine if you can choose any two of them so that their sum is greater or equal to 10.

The answer is YES if a_i \ge 10 holds, where a_i is the i-th element.

Input

The first line contains a single integer t (1 \leq t \leq 1000) — the number of test cases.

The only line of each test case contains three digits a, b, c (0 \leq a, b, c \leq 9).

Output

Output YES if you can choose any two such that their sum is \geq 10, and NO otherwise.

Example
Input
3
1 4 3
Output
YES
NO
Note

In the first test case, 4 + 3 = 7. Also raw math: $$$x \le 10^5$$$ stays untouched.
